title: All City Mile × Rebel Relays
operatingContext: New Balance field marketing · community event · product launch
summary: New Balance revived Seattle’s All City Mile at UW Husky Track in 2025. The sold-out event welcomed 300+ runners across eight heats and relays, supported by 30+ volunteers, and raised $5,000 for Girls on the Run.
insight: Seattle runners still cared about the All City Mile, a community event that had been inactive for several years. New Balance needed an introduction to its new Rebel shoe that felt rooted in local running culture.
intention: Revive a beloved local event while creating an authentic setting for runners to experience the New Balance Rebel and supporting Girls on the Run.
opportunity: Pair a new running shoe launch with the return of an established community event, giving runners a reason to race, gather, and try the product.
idea: Bring the All City Mile back to UW Husky Track as a race-like community expo, with multiple heats, partner activations, and a Rebel-only relay.
role: As New Balance Field Marketing Specialist, I conceptualized, planned, and executed the event. I cultivated the partner network, led event logistics and volunteer coordination, and helped shape the event identity and promotion.
experience: A month-long campaign used New Balance, partner, and personal channels. A pre-event Intro to Rebel run helped build momentum. On race day, eight heats made space for runners of different abilities; a relay required participants to wear the Rebel. Shokz, Nuun, Super Jock ’n Jill, CSRD, and Athletic Form contributed partner activations. More than 30 volunteers supported operations.

metrics.label: raised for Girls on the Run

chapters.title: A race-day format with room to gather
chapters.body: The event included a kids’ dash and a relay that gave runners another chance to try the Rebel. Recovery stations and run-form clinics added practical value for participants.

title: Your Mothers Run Crew
editorialTitle: Building a Community People Return To
clientPlatform: Your Mothers Run Crew × New Balance × Goop × Little Words Project
operatingContext: Founder-led community · owned brand · brand partnerships
summary: I founded Your Mothers Run Crew in Austin as a women-only monthly running community built around the buddy system before and after dark. In 2024, I led sold-out New Balance collaborations with Goop and Little Words Project, pairing a run or walk with distinct in-store gatherings.
insight: Women running before or after dark can benefit from a community that makes looking out for one another part of the ritual.
intention: Create a recurring, welcoming run community and extend its social ritual through relevant partner experiences.
opportunity: A monthly run followed by a gathering could turn a shared running practice into a durable community and a platform for collaboration.
idea: I founded the crew, developed its logo and brand strategy, and shaped a monthly run-and-gather format that grew from post-run dumplings to panels and brand collaborations.
role: I founded and led the community, created its logo and brand strategy, and served as planner, community lead, and liaison among the brands. I proposed the concepts and marketing execution plans for both activations.
experience: The crew paired its monthly run with a gathering afterward, growing from post-run dumplings into panels and brand collaborations. In 2024, the community hosted sold-out New Balance collaborations with Goop and Little Words Project.

title: Freaks of Nature × Alba Optics × Runaway Milano
clientPlatform: Freaks of Nature × Alba Optics × Runaway Milano
operatingContext: Independent brand collaboration · community event · content production
summary: For Freaks of Nature, I coordinated a Milan community event with Alba Optics and local running store Runaway Milano. A sold-out 50-place morning run paired two short-form videos with an outdoor-inspired gathering at Runaway Milano.
insight: Freaks of Nature and Milan-based Alba Optics shared an outdoor-minded audience, while Runaway Milano brought an established local running community.
intention: Introduce Freaks of Nature to runners in Milan through a locally grounded collaboration and create social content around the community event.
opportunity: A local running store and an aligned Milan eyewear brand could make the collaboration relevant to runners while connecting the partners’ communities.
idea: The “Back In Bed — Eat, Sleep, Run” concept brought a dawn run together with Alba Optics’ bed-and-surfboard van installation, product demos, giveaways, coffee, and croissants.
role: Working through Katherine Kalill Productions on behalf of Freaks of Nature, I coordinated the community event and delivered two reels: an event introduction and a recap.
experience: The February 20 event started at Runaway Milano with 50 spots and sold out. Participants received custom tees for a route past Milan’s Olympic Torch before returning for the van photo moment, product demos, Freaks of Nature samples and giveaways, coffee, and croissants. Alba Optics supplied the branded van experience; Runaway Milano provided the local store and community setting.

title: Mom, You Deserve Your Flowers
editorialTitle: Bridging Fashion Culture With a Passion for High Performance
operatingContext: New Balance community event leadership · community partnership · product trial
summary: For New Balance, I developed a Mother’s Day partnership with Seattle gym Athletic Form to introduce a Hyrox audience to running shoes. The May 10, 2025 event sold out and paired shoe demos and a high-energy workout with bouquets, custom event branding, and brunch.
insight: Athletic Form’s Hyrox community included running in its training, making it a relevant audience for race-day shoes. The Mother’s Day setting also made room for recognition through a shared workout and the gesture of giving flowers.
intention: Create an event that connected New Balance running shoes with a new local audience through a welcoming, celebratory experience.
opportunity: A Mother’s Day gathering could bridge Athletic Form’s Hyrox community and New Balance’s running range through shared movement and thoughtful hospitality.
idea: “Mom, You Deserve Your Flowers” combined a Hyrox workout and shoe demos with a build-your-own bouquet area, a limited custom tee drop, a DJ, and brunch.
role: As New Balance Community Event Leader, I developed the Athletic Form partnership, pitched the concept, created its branding and graphics, designed a limited 200-shirt drop, planned the event and ticketing workflow, and coordinated activation details.
experience: Guests could try New Balance shoes, take part in a high-energy Hyrox workout, build a bouquet, and gather for brunch with a DJ. Katherine coordinated signage, release timing, ticket sales, and partner touchpoints. The event generated more than 60 organic social posts; Athletic Form received professional event photos and video for community use.

title: Women’s Self-Defense Initiative
editorialTitle: Using Brand Purpose to Create Practical Impact
operatingContext: New Balance event management · retail partnership · women’s community programming
summary: For New Balance, I planned and managed a March 16, 2025 women’s self-defense event with REI in Seattle. Timed within REI’s member-sale weekend and the launch of the Hierro trail shoe, it paired a demo run with a runner-focused self-defense class and sold out.
insight: A trail shoe launch and Women’s History Month created an opportunity to offer women runners a useful community experience alongside product trial.
intention: Help participants feel welcomed and cared for while introducing New Balance’s new Hierro trail shoe in a relevant retail setting.
opportunity: Pair a product demo with practical instruction, community leaders, and retail staff preparation during REI’s existing sale weekend.
idea: A demo run with New Balance Hierro shoes led into a self-defense class designed for runners, with REI, CSRD, local community leaders, and women-owned businesses involved.
role: As New Balance event manager, I pitched the initiative and led its planning and execution: coordinating with REI and community groups, arranging the class and event details, developing graphics, preparing brand touchpoints, and seeding community leaders.
experience: The sold-out March 16, 2025 event in Seattle paired a Hierro demo run with a runner-focused self-defense class. Katherine coordinated REI and community partners, event details, and New Balance brand touchpoints. REI hosted during its member-sale weekend; the New Balance sales comparison is reported separately as concurrent retail performance.

metrics.label: year-over-year increase in New Balance sales at REI Seattle in March 2025 vs March 2024; concurrent with the event, not attributed to it

chapters.title: Make the program useful to runners
chapters.body: The self-defense instructor brought 30 years of experience. Community leaders served as pacers, and the event also included women-owned businesses, personal-safety alarms, and support from Poppi.

chapters.title: Keep retail performance in context
chapters.body: New Balance sales at REI Seattle were reported 225% higher in March 2025 than in March 2024. The comparison is concurrent with the event; it is not presented as an event-attributed result.

title: Joie Baby × For All Mothers

title: USA Track Championships
